subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron isolated sessions get their own `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or keep the current per-job `toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards only?
rationale: This defines a scheduled-run tool-execution security boundary and likely adds public config surface, so automation should not choose the permanent precedence or compatibility behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add cron-specific policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, then document and test fresh-install and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat isolated cron sessions as covered by `tools.subagents.tools`, reducing config surface but coupling cron and subagent semantics.

options.title: Keep current safeguards
options.body: Leave cron control to per-job `toolsAllow` and duplicate-delivery safeguards, which keeps config smaller but does not solve the requested operator deny boundary.

recommendation.title: Add cron-specific policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, then document and test fresh-install and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior issue review and recent cron delivery/security-adjacent history make `steipete` the best available decision owner.
